newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power steady amid plant outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power steady amid plant outages.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. held steady amid scattered regional power plant outages despite unseasonably mild weather, market sources said Thursday.
"Prices firmed up last night and that is carrying over to today," said one California trader.
Recent unplanned outages include a 750 megawatt (MW) unit at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Arizona and a 500 MW unit at the Jim Bridger plant in Wyoming.
Both were expected to return to service Thursday night.

A 755 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired plant, which had been down since the weekend, was restarting early Thursday, but a smaller 187 MW unit at the New Mexico plant was shut for repairs to a boiler tube.
The 1,221 MW unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona began ramping down for a 50-day refueling outage which will start February 22.
The 1,080 unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was expected to restart late this month after a refueling outage was extended for extra maintenance.

The Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures 3 to 6 degrees F above average through Sunday, while the Southwest was expected to see temperatures warm from 2 to 4 degrees above normal on Thursday to 4 to 8 degrees above normal on Sunday, according to Weather Services Corp.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Friday was quoted at $12.00-$12.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $12.00-13.50 for Thursday.
Firm, off-peak COB deliveries for Friday were quoted at $7.50-8.00, up from $7.00-7.50.
Firm, peak electricity at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) for Friday was quoted at $10.50-11.50, compared with $11.00-11.75 for Thursday.
Off-peak Mid-C for day-ahead delivery was quoted at $5.75-6.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was quoted at $15.00-16.00, while off-peak deliveries held at $7.00-9.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $14.00-15.00 unchanged from Thursday, while off-peak remained at $7.00-9.00.
